messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: MSstats normalization
parts:
Dear Gene,

Thank you for your question.
1. to turn off the normalization, use 'normalization=FALSE' As you mentioned, if you already external normalization function in log2 scale, 'normalization=FALSE' will not do anything for normalization, just will reformat for fitting the model next step.
2. about log transformation : MSstats now has only two possibility for log transformation, logTrans=2 or 10. Now logTrans=FALSE is not available. I will update it soon. If you want to use before I update, there is the temporary solution. After you applied an external normalization function, 'Intensity' column has normalization and log2 scaled values. Then please just recalculate 2^(Intensity) in 'Intensity' column. below is the simple code for that.

------------------------
## I assume the name of raw file is 'Msstats.input.annotate'
Msstats.input.annotate$Intensity<-2^(MSstats.input.annotate$Intensity)
data1<-dataProcess(Msstats.input.annotate, normalization=FALSE)
------------------------

I hope it will help for you.

Thanks,
Meena

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MSstats normalization
parts:
Dear Priyanka,

Could you check whether your input data has 0 intensities? Log(0) = - infinity, and these infinite values can create trouble for the downstream analysis. If this is the case, you can either replace 0 with small values, or with NA - depending on what makes sense for your  data. If this is not the case, could you please attach your msstats.log file, so that we can take a look?

Also, it is best to use Msstats.daily available at http://www.msstats.org/installation.html

Best wishes
Olga

Dear Priyanka,

First of all, I'm so sorry for late response. I will try to response asap for next questions.

and thank you for sharing your data. It is easy for me to answer your problem.
1. about message : Removed 1 rows containing non-finite values (stat_boxplot)
     ---> You don't need to worry about this error message. When you have any missing value (intensity=NA), the package for plot (ggplot2) always reports this message. However, it doesn't mean that your data have problem. Please ignore this error message (I report this error message in 'Known issues in MSstats' document.

2. about upper limit in y-axis for QC plot
     ---> Thank you for reporting this issue. 'dataProcessPlots' function has the option 'ylimUp' which can set up upper limit of y-axis. default is 30. That is why it show only 0 to 30 log2 transformed intensities. So, when I set up ylimUp=40 ( such as dataProcessPlots(quant, type="QCPlot", ylimUp=40) ), I got the all intensities. If you want to see more option for dataProcessPlots, please use ?dataProcessPlots, then it will show you details.

3. about new error message as "Subject : 1, Condition : Mutant-18055 has multiple rows (duplicate rows) for some features ()"
    ---> What I found from your data is there is no Peptide information at all as attached captures. So, If you put any information in 'PeptideSequence' column, it should work. (I tested it, it worked.) If you still had the problem, please let me know.


I hope it will be helpful for you. Welcome to any further question.

Meena

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MSstats normalization
parts:
Dear Priyanka,

MSstats decides statistical significance not only based on the fold change, but also based on the associated estimate of variation (called standard error). If a larger fold change has larger associated variation, then it can be an artifact of random chance, and the protein is viewed as not statistically significant. Please take a look at the column 'standard error' in the MSstats output to see the estimates of variation. You can find more details in this paper http://www.biomedcentral.com/1471-2105/13/S16/S6/abstract

I hope this helps
Sincerely
Olga

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MSstats normalization
parts:
Dear Priyanka,

It is best to generate residual plots on normalized data. Otherwise, deviations from the expected pattern can be due to both a need for normalization and a need for unequal variance.

For large-scale DDA experiments, interference=FALSE, equalFeatureVar=FALSE are good assumptions. They mean that you assume that a protein can have features of varying quality, and that most interferences are noise (i.e. they will not be reproduced if you repeat the experiment).

There is something wrong with the residual plot in the file ProteinX_QuantileUnequalVar.png. If you look at the range of the predicted values (x axis), you see that the values are very small, and are centered around 0. Most likely you normalized the residuals, and tried to re-fit the model to the residuals instead of the log-intensities. I suggest that you quit R to clean all the memory, and repeat the process of normalization, model fitting and residual plots once again.

The time course design means that in your data subjects with identical labels are present in multiple groups. Check your input dataset, and make sure that each replicate has a unique id, regardless of the strain.

I hope this helps
Sincerely
Olga
